original_witness: Active values [10,18,25,31,40] sort to the same order; the unique middle value is 25.
updated_witness: Replace only the fourth record value 31 with 16. The values sort to [10,16,18,25,40], whose unique middle value is 18.
rationale: Both odd rosters have exactly one rank-3 value, and the single corrected record moves the median from 25 to 18.

original_witness: Effective capacities are stage A 100*0.80=80, stage B 100*0.90=90, and stage C 120*0.75=90; A is the unique bottleneck at 80.
updated_witness: Replace only stage B's factor 0.90 with 0.70. Effective capacities become 80,70,90, so B is the unique bottleneck at 70.
rationale: Taking the minimum of the three computed capacities gives a unique but different bottleneck before and after the one-factor correction.

original_witness: For 41 items, usable capacity 10, and cost 7 per container, ceil(41/10)=5 containers cost 35.
updated_witness: Replace only usable capacity 10 with 14. Then ceil(41/14)=3 containers cost 21.
rationale: The ceiling operation uniquely fixes the whole-container count on both sides of the single capacity correction.

original_witness: A serial process starts with 1000 units and has yields 0.80 and 0.50, giving 1000*0.80*0.50=400 units.
updated_witness: Replace only the second-stage yield 0.50 with 0.75; output is 1000*0.80*0.75=600 units.
rationale: The frozen serial-product rule yields one numerical output before and after replacement of a single factor.

original_witness: Two entries of 90 and 50 are both classed ordinary, so the signed balance is 90+50=140.
updated_witness: Replace only the 50 entry's class with contra; its sign reverses and the balance is 90-50=40.
changed_node: Formal class of the 50 entry: ordinary -> contra.
rationale: Exactly one entry changes sign under the closed-world class rule; no amount or other class changes.

original_witness: A tax-inclusive gross of 120 at rate 20% has base 120/(1+0.20)=100.
updated_witness: Replace only the applicable rate 20% with 25%; the same gross has base 120/(1+0.25)=96.
rationale: Inverting the fixed inclusive-gross equation produces a unique base at either positive rate.

original_witness: A 120 km trip split equally between speeds 30 and 60 uses 60/30+60/60=3 hours, so average speed is 40.
updated_witness: Replace only the distance ratio 1:1 with 1:3 while total distance stays 120. Times are 30/30+90/60=2.5 hours, so average speed is 48.
rationale: Fixed total distance and positive speeds determine each leg distance, total time, and hence one average speed under each ratio.

original_witness: From 100 units, a 50% initial acceptance gives 50; one permitted 50% rework pass adds 25, totaling 75.
updated_witness: Replace only the permitted rework-pass count 1 with 2; the second pass adds 12.5, totaling 87.5.
rationale: The finite recurrence is deterministic, and the only new term comes from the one corrected pass-count record.

original_witness: For key ABCD, active prefixes A->Red, AB->Blue, and ABC->Green all match; the unique longest match ABC selects Green.
updated_witness: Remove only the ABC->Green table entry. Of the unchanged matches, AB is uniquely longest and selects Blue.
changed_node: Most-specific routing-table entry ABC->Green: active -> removed.
rationale: Prefix lengths 1,2,3 are strictly ordered, so both the original and next-longest active match are unique.

original_witness: Candidates 2.1.0-alpha and 2.1.0-beta have equal numeric cores; lexical prerelease comparison makes beta the unique later version.
updated_witness: Replace only the first candidate's prerelease identifier alpha with rc. Under the same explicit lexical rule, rc is later than beta.
changed_node: First candidate prerelease identifier: alpha -> rc.
rationale: The numeric components tie and the unequal identifiers create exactly one decisive comparison in each state.

original_witness: Center 50 and half-width 1 give [49,51], whose endpoints both lie in the acceptance band [48,52], so it is fully contained.
updated_witness: Replace only half-width 1 with 3, giving [47,53]. It intersects [48,52] but is not fully contained, so the exhaustive rules label it partial overlap.
rationale: Endpoint comparison places each closed-interval state in exactly one of the three explicitly exhaustive relation labels.

original_witness: With | as delimiter and backslash escaping the following delimiter, red\|blue|green|gold parses as [red|blue, green, gold]; field 2 is green.
updated_witness: Remove only the escape marker before the first |. The raw record red|blue|green|gold parses as [red, blue, green, gold]; field 2 is blue.
changed_node: Escape marker immediately before the first delimiter: present -> absent.
rationale: A deterministic left-to-right parse under the supplied escape rule gives one ordered field list in each state.

original_witness: For ratio 100 labeled a power ratio, the supplied encoding is 10*log10(100)=20.
updated_witness: Replace only the quantity type power with amplitude; the supplied encoding is then 20*log10(100)=40.
rationale: The fixed ratio has log10 value 2; the single metadata selector uniquely chooses multiplier 10 or 20.

original_witness: The closed lookup table maps (UDP,53)->Gamma and (TCP,53)->Delta. Header (UDP,53) uniquely selects Gamma.
updated_witness: Replace only the header protocol UDP with TCP while port 53 remains. Tuple (TCP,53) uniquely selects Delta.
rationale: The protocol-port tuple is an exact table key, and the two distinct keys map to one distinct label each without outside knowledge.

original_witness: Requested bits 111 under mask 010 give 111 AND NOT 010 = 101.
updated_witness: Replace only the mask 010 with 011; 111 AND NOT 011 = 100.
rationale: Bitwise complement and conjunction are deterministic for all three fixed bit positions.

original_witness: If day 1 is Monday, Thursdays fall on 4,11,18,25; the third Thursday is day 18.
updated_witness: Replace only the weekday of day 1 with Wednesday. Thursdays fall on 2,9,16,23,30; the third is day 16.
changed_node: Weekday assigned to the month's first day: Monday -> Wednesday.
rationale: Advancing dates modulo seven from the fixed month anchor yields exactly one third occurrence in either state.

original_witness: Agents A,B,C allow {1},{1,2},{2,3}. Exhausting all 3! assignments leaves only (A,B,C)=(1,2,3).
updated_witness: Replace A's complete allowed-item record {1} with {3}; B and C remain {1,2} and {2,3}. Exhausting all 3! assignments leaves only (3,1,2).
rationale: All six bijections were checked in each state; exactly one satisfies every complete allowance row before and after the atomic row replacement.

original_witness: Interval A starts at 2 with length 8, so A=[2,10]; B=[5,8]. A contains B under the stated relation rules.
updated_witness: Replace only A's length 8 with 2, so A=[2,4] while B=[5,8]. A is now strictly before B.
rationale: The explicit endpoint inequalities make contains, before, and overlap mutually exclusive for these two states.

original_witness: The pass rule requires support weight at least 7 and every veto member to vote yes. Non-veto yes weights 4+3=7, while veto member P (weight 2) votes no; the proposal fails.
updated_witness: Replace only P's vote no with yes. Support becomes 9 and the sole veto conjunct is satisfied, so the proposal passes.
changed_node: Certified vote of veto member P: no -> yes.
rationale: The threshold and veto conjunction have definite truth values; changing one recorded vote flips the uniquely determined decision.

original_witness: Parallel prerequisite tasks A=2 and B=4 must both finish before C=3. Completion is max(2,4)+3=7.
updated_witness: Replace only A's duration 2 with 5. The same graph completes at max(5,4)+3=8.
rationale: The fixed DAG has one join and deterministic earliest-finish recurrence; the corrected duration also switches the critical predecessor.

original_witness: Among X,Y,Z, pairwise records say X beats Y, X beats Z, and Y beats Z. X alone beats every opponent and is the Condorcet winner.
updated_witness: Replace only the X-versus-Y record with Y beats X. With unchanged Y beats Z, Y alone now beats every opponent.
changed_node: Pairwise outcome X versus Y: X beats Y -> Y beats X.
rationale: Checking each of the three candidates against both opponents gives exactly one all-opponent winner in each tournament.

original_witness: Conflict sets {A,B} and {B,C} are both hit by singleton {B}; neither {A} nor {C} hits both, so {B} is the unique minimum hitting set.
updated_witness: Replace only {B,C} with {A,C}. Singleton {A} hits {A,B} and {A,C}; neither {B} nor {C} hits both, so {A} is uniquely minimum.
rationale: All singleton subsets were checked; a size-one solution exists uniquely in each state, so all larger hitting sets are nonminimal.

original_witness: For A,B,C,D, constraints A first, B immediately before C, and D after C admit only ABCD among all 4! sequences.
updated_witness: Replace only the adjacency clue with C immediately before B; A-first and D-after-C stay fixed. Exhausting all 4! sequences leaves only ACBD.
changed_node: Complete adjacency clue: B immediately before C -> C immediately before B.
rationale: All 24 permutations were evaluated against the three constraints in each state, producing one different satisfying arrangement.

original_witness: Over attributes {P,Q,R}, dependencies R->Q and Q->P give closure R+={R,Q,P}; Q lacks R and P lacks Q,R, so {R} is the unique minimal key.
updated_witness: Replace only R->Q with Q->R while Q->P remains. Then Q+={Q,R,P}; R and P cannot reach all attributes, so {Q} is the unique minimal key.
changed_node: One complete functional-dependency record: R->Q -> Q->R.
rationale: Closures of every subset of {P,Q,R} were enumerated; exactly one singleton is a key in each state, and the empty set is not.
